newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil global retires $2.7 bln in Bradies - cenbank.
newsitem.headline: Brazil global retires $2.7 bln in Bradies - cenbank.

text.p: Brazil's $3.0 billion 30-year global bond deal will allow it to retire $2.716 billion in old Brady bonds, a Central Bank official said.
Linaldo Aguiar, head of the bank's external debt department, said the debt swap deal would also give Brazil a net financial gain of some $220 million.

Aguiar told reporters this "rough calculation" reflected gains through reduced external debt, the freeing up of collateral, and the differences in interest rate payments on the old debt and the new paper.
According to the latest Central Bank figures, Brazil's total stock of restructured Brady debt before the global and debt swap deal amounted to $43.9 billion.
Brazil on Wednesday exchanged $3.0 billion of uncollaterized 30-year bonds for $1.622 billion of discount bonds, $542 million of par bonds, $86 million of C bonds and $750 million in cash.

Aguiar said the $750 million in cash, of which $426,342 will be used to buy back pars and $713,540 to buy back discount, would be used to either retire domestic or external debt, as required by Senate authorization for such operations.
Some $605.46 million of freed-up collateral from the retired Bradies would also be used eventually to retire debt, he added.
The zero-coupon U.S. Treasuries, which had been held as collateral will return to Brazil on Monday.

"This value will be transferred into cash at an opportune moment," Aguiar said. "It is our right to give no hint as to what our strategy will be with these securities," he added when asked if they would be sold quickly.
